metadata.note: The Green Bay Route: the Green Bay and Western Railroad and the companies before it - the Green Bay and Lake Pepin (1866, renamed Green Bay and Minnesota 9 Sep 1873), the Green Bay, Winona and St. Paul (operating 14 Oct 1881 - 10 Jun 1896) and the Green Bay and Western (from 10 Jun 1896) - plus its Kewaunee, Green Bay and Western, Ahnapee and Western and Waupaca-Green Bay affiliates. Drawn from research/branches/green_bay_and_western_railroad.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains) (2026-10-06). Before this layer the map drew no GB&W route at all. Only the report's drawable spans are drawn. Rule 4 splits: the main line, the Winona approaches and the La Crosse Division are split at 14 Oct 1881 and 10 Jun 1896 into features sharing identical geometry, one per operating company (the 1873 Lake Pepin -> Minnesota rename is the same corporation and is not split). The Kewaunee line is split at GB&W control (28 Jun 1897) and the Ahnapee and Western at GB&W control (12 Nov 1906). Last GB&W passenger train April 1949; the Feb 1952 Official Guide prints both the GB&W and the KGB&W as 'Freight Service only'. Green Bay terminal: drawn to the GB&W's west-bank stub terminal (Norwood side), not Washington Street. The Winona approach is era-specific: C&NW track and bridge 1874-1891 (drawn as its own feature on the C&NW grade and the C&NW bridge, located from OHM, the OSM Flyway Trail and a surviving disused bridge span), the Winona Bridge Railway from 1 Sep 1891.
sources: https://blog.greenbayroute.com/1948ett.htm (1948 employee timetable; 'Passenger service ended on April 4, 1949')
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitehall_station_(Wisconsin) (last train Apr 13 1949, citing Winona Daily News Apr 14 1949)
https://doorcounty.substack.com/p/after-stormy-start-railroad-served (Door County Advocate, Jun 10 1976: 'even limited passenger service was dropped in 1936')
https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/wisconsinrrs.pdf (John Fowler, Wisconsin passenger stations: GB&W section 132, A&W 120, Scandinavia - Waupaca 133 'b: 1920RG', KGB&W 138)
Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt ~line 54031-54112): GB&W and KGB&W both '(Freight Service only.)'
metadata.geometry_method: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (mail.ru mirror, cached degree tiles) plus OpenHistoricalMap (CC0) for lifted grades, traced with opstrace.py: Dijkstra over all railway ways; the GB&W's own grade (members of the CN Whitehall Subdivision, Plover Subdivision, Luxemburg Branch and GB&W Waupaca Branch route relations, ways tagged old_railway_operator=Green Bay and Western / Ahnapee and Western, the Newton Blackmour, Tomorrow River and Ahnapee State Trails, and OHM ways labelled Green Bay and Western / Kewaunee, Green Bay and Western / Ahnapee and Western / Green Bay, Winona & St Paul) costed 1x, untagged rail 1.25x, cycleways 3x, any other named operator 12x; waypoints from the research report's via lists, each geocode's type checked and the bad ones (Seymour, Royalton, Scranton, Dodge, Trempealeau, Kewaunee, Waupaca returned towns or counties) hand-pinned. Straight-line legs: the Winona Bridge Railway river crossing (0.67 mi) and a Marshland junction connector on the La Crosse Division (0.49 mi); branch-to-main joins under 300 m at Plover, Scandinavia and Casco Junction. OHM dates were never copied into segments.
not_yet_sourced: End years that are the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end ([OPEN]): La Crosse Division 1896 (the true end lies between 1896 and the 26 Oct 1922 abandonment of Onalaska - La Crosse; a 1900s-1910s Official Guide would settle it); Stevens Point Branch 1896 (true end between 1896 and the 1944 ETT, which shows it freight only).
Start year that is the first full year, not a proven first train: the Marshland - Winona C&NW-bridge approach from 1874 (the line reached Marshland Dec 1873).

[ANCHOR] Waupaca Branch (Waupaca-Green Bay Railway): only 1920 is proven (Fowler, 1920 Russell's Guide). First and last passenger years unknown; construction '1907, 1913' suggests it may have reached Waupaca only in 1913.

CONFLICT, Arcadia - Marshland/East Winona opening: greenbayroute and the Marshland article put the GB&M through to Marshland/East Winona in Dec 1873; Wikipedia lists 'Arcadia - East Winona opened 1883', and OHM dates the GB&W Arcadia - East Winona grade to 1883. Drawn from 1873 per the report. If 1883 is the line's own opening, the 1873-1882 Arcadia - Marshland years are overstated or drawn on a later alignment.
CONFLICT, last main-line train: 4 Apr 1949 (greenbayroute) vs 13 Apr 1949 (Winona Daily News, via Wikipedia's Whitehall station article). Year 1949 either way.
CONFLICT, Kewaunee Division end: 1937 (greenbayroute, drawn) vs an unverified 1941.
CONFLICT, Sturgeon Bay Division end: 1936 (Door County Advocate 1976, drawn) vs 1937 (other web summaries).
Kewaunee, Green Bay and Western 1892-1897: who operated the trains (the KGB&W itself or the GBW&StP) is not established; drawn under the KGB&W's own company name and colour.
Ahnapee and Western 1892-1906: whether A&W trains ran through to Green Bay over the KGB&W is not established; drawn from Casco Junction only.

Winona: the GB&M/GB&W's own Winona station site (pre-1891, which trains backed into) and the exact Winona Bridge Railway landing points were not located; both approaches end at the Winona riverfront and the WBR bridge is a straight line.
Every headway_min and avg_speed_kmh in this layer is an estimate; no speed was measured from a timetable.
branches_deliberately_omitted: Iola Branch, Scandinavia - Iola (Iola & Northern, 4.7 mi, 1893-1958): 'train service' began July 1893 and Fowler lists Iola as a station, but no timetable year confirms a passenger train, and the 1944 and 1948 ETTs show it freight only. Report drawable: NONE.
Biron spur, Wisconsin Rapids - Coyne - Biron (2.23 mi): Fowler marks Coyne and Biron 'b pass?' (passenger service doubtful); paper-mill spur with no confirmed passenger year. Report drawable: NONE.

Green Bay, Stevens Point and Northern as a separate company (Jan - Aug 1882): leased to the GBW&StP within months and not shown to have run its own trains; the Stevens Point Branch is drawn as GBW&StP throughout.
La Crosse Division after June 1896 (GB&W era): no post-1896 passenger year is proven, so no GB&W-coloured La Crosse feature is drawn.
freight_only_excluded: OG1952: 'GREEN BAY AND WESTERN RAILROAD. (Freight Service only.)' and 'KEWAUNEE, GREEN BAY AND WESTERN RAILROAD. (Freight Service only.)' - nothing past April 1949 is drawn.
Kewaunee Division after 1937 and Sturgeon Bay Division after 1936; the Ahnapee and Western under Sturgeon Bay owners from 1947 (freight only, to 1986).
Stevens Point, Waupaca and Iola branches in the 1940s (freight only in the 1944 ETT).
Onalaska - La Crosse track 1896-1922: kept to the last confirmed passenger year (1896).
Fox Valley & Western (from 1993) and the Fox Valley & Lake Superior: freight successors, never drawn.

segments.note: New London - Grand Rapids (Wisconsin Rapids) opened January 1873 and the line reached Merrillan, Arcadia and East Winona in December 1873, so for 1873 the western half is drawn for a year in which it ran only from December. Arcadia - Marshland is drawn from 1873 following the research report (greenbayroute: the line reached East Winona 18 Dec 1873), but Wikipedia lists 'Arcadia - East Winona opened 1883' - an unresolved CONFLICT, recorded in metadata.not_yet_sourced. The company was the Green Bay and Lake Pepin until 9 Sep 1873 and the Green Bay and Minnesota after (same corporation). Trains ran on into Winona over C&NW track - see the separate C&NW-bridge feature. The Mar 1878 timetable shows an Accommodation and a Passenger each way daily except Sunday. Ends 14 Oct 1881 (GBW&StP takeover). Headway is an estimate from the number of trains in the cited timetables, not a measured figure; avg_speed_kmh is NOT sourced.
sources: Segment-level: opening dates from Wikipedia and greenbayroute; through service proven by the Mar 1878 timetable. The Arcadia - Marshland start year is in conflict (1873 vs 1883). Headway estimated.

segments.note: Green Bay and Western Railroad, incorporated 3 Jun 1896, began operating 10 Jun 1896. Passengers peaked at 310,000 in 1915. Through trains Green Bay - Winona via New London, Wisconsin Rapids and Merrillan. Headway is an estimate from the number of trains in the cited timetables, not a measured figure; avg_speed_kmh is NOT sourced.
sources: Segment-level: the 1896 start is the GB&W's first operating day (greenbayroute chronology); the ridership figure is from greenbayroute. Headway estimated - the 1896-1943 train count was not checked year by year.

segments.note: By the May 1944 employee timetable the service was mixed trains on the New London and Whitehall divisions; in 1948 mixed trains 5/6 and 7/8 ran daily, and fast freights 1/2 carried passengers on alternate days. Fewer than 1,000 passengers in 1947. The ICC allowed discontinuance and the last passenger train ran in April 1949 - 4 April per greenbayroute, 13 April per the Winona Daily News of 14 Apr 1949 (a conflict of days, not of year). The Feb 1952 Official Guide prints the GB&W as 'Freight Service only'. Freight continued (GB&W, then the Fox Valley & Western from 1993) and is not drawn.
sources: Segment-level: the 1944 ETT and the 1948 ETT (which states the April 1949 end) establish the mixed-train service and its end; the Whitehall station article gives the 13 Apr date; the Feb 1952 Guide confirms freight only. Headway is an estimate.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] One proven year only: Fowler marks Knutsons, Rowes and Granite with 'b' = the 1920 Russell's Guide, the only dated passenger evidence for this branch.
